messages:
Ivy: quick sync 3: I'm assembling a small 'tenant fallback playbook' section for the Dedicated provisioning guide. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/612 (WIP). Need: terragrunt+terraform examples, exact SLA phrasing for fallback, and one-liner CLI workflow for live migrations.

Jon: copying infra folks. can we show a minimal terraform snippet that creates a reserved_pool and attaches a tenant label? Ops always asks for a copy-paste.

Ivy: yes. adding a tiny terraform block below for reviewer eyeballs. kept it minimal so it can live in the guide: 
```hcl
resource "redwood_reserved_pool" "acme_pool" {
  name        = "acme-reserved"
  gpu_type    = "A100-80GB"
  capacity    = 10
  labels      = { team = "acme" }
}

resource "redwood_tenant" "acme" {
  id = "acme"
  reserved_pool_id = redwood_reserved_pool.acme_pool.id
  burst_policy = jsonencode({ max_burst = 100 })
}
```

Priya: can you also add a terragrunt snippet showing how to parametrize the pool per-stage? I'll drop that in after lunch.

Ivy: please do. also adding a tiny CLI migration example (for customers that want to move from hosted to dedicated live):
```bash
# export keys
export REDWOOD_KEY=...
# create tenant + attach pool
redwoodctl tenants create --id acme --reserved-pool acme-reserved
# warm-up: send low-traffic health-checks for 5m
redwoodctl tenants probe --id acme --duration 5m
# flip route in dns or gateway
# monitor token/latency in console
```

Samir: SLA wording note: do NOT call "degraded throughput" an SLA. We have two separate guarantees: latency SLOs for Dedicated when capacity is met, and availability SLA for Reserved Pools only when the pool is healthy and not preempted. I'll propose exact wording in a small commit.

Jon: also include a short "what to expect" bullet list for customers migrating:
- brief warm-up period for KV caches (1-5 min)
- first few requests may hit cold kv -> slightly higher latency
- reserved_pool precedence, but preemption windows can move some nodes to shared pool
- automatic fallback path: reserved_pool -> shared_pool -> slowed_throughput (not an SLA outage)

Ivy: added that list inline. docs-bot 4: link-checker run on branch found one broken anchor: /dedicated/provisioning#old-eviction-model -> 404.

docs-bot: Suggestion: add a short redirect or update anchor to /dedicated/provisioning#eviction-model-v2.

Priya: pushed terragrunt param example and a small note about terraform variables.

Ivy: thanks! updated the PR with the terragrunt snippet and the terraform block. also added a short annotated eviction example: 
```text
Annotated eviction order (simple):
1) Node A: reserved pool resources exhausted -> new tenant pods scheduled to shared pool
2) Node B: preemption window opens -> low-priority pods on Node B evicted
3) Tenant in reserved_pool may get thundering-start but will preferentially be scheduled back to reserved nodes when they free up
```

Samir: I ran the phrasing through legal for the SLA lines. Small change: replace "Reserved Pools only when the pool is healthy" with "Reserved Pools are SLA-backed when allocated capacity meets the committed size and no preemption event is active." will push commit.

Ivy: small CI hiccup earlier: the link-checker flagged /sdk/go/provisioning-example -> 404. fixed path in snippets to /sdk/go/dedicated/provision.

Jon: LGTM on the terraform snippet. I'll add a tiny note in the ops runbook about verifying tenant labels post-provision.

Priya: smoke-tested the CLI steps on staging and the probe command returns expected warm-up metrics. left one nit about wording on 'warm-up' timeframe.

Ivy: great. target to merge by Tuesday AM after one more pass from Samir on SLA phrasing and a final smoke from Priya. If anything else surfaces, drop commits on the PR. :shipit:

Samir: will add the SLA commit this afternoon. thanks team!
